newsitem.title: UK: Reuters third-quarter revenue up 9 percent.
newsitem.headline: Reuters third-quarter revenue up 9 percent.

text.p: International news and information organisation Reuters Holdings Plc said Friday its third-quarter revenue rose 9 percent, while sales of its new 3000 product series had met expectations so far.
The company said third-quarter revenue reached 736 million pounds ($1.17 billion), up from 677 million pounds ($1.08 billion) in the third quarter of 1995.

Excluding exchange rate movements, growth was 10 percent in the third quarter, while revenue for the first nine months increased by 10 percent to 2.174 billion pounds ($3.46 billion) against 1.972 billion pounds ($3.14 billion) in the 1995 period.
"The sales rate of our 3000 range of products, launched in July, has met our expectations so far," Chief Executive Peter Job said in a statement.

"The response from those clients who have begun using the 3000 series, which adds extensive databases and analytics to our real-time services, has been positive. These early signs are encouraging but we need to maintain this initial momentum to translate interest into significant additional revenue," he said.

Reuter shares, which had been trading down nine pence ahead of the announcement, turned around to stand five pence higher at 777-1/2p at midday. Reuter American Depositary Receipts were up $1.375 at $74.625 on Nasdaq in mid-morning trading.
"We had been looking for revenues up between seven or nine percent so that was a good figure. Also, the statement on product sales and streamlining was quite encouraging," one trader in London said.
The third-quarter revenue growth showed a rise in installations of information management systems after the lower levels recorded in the first six months.

Reuters said it also saw increasing demand for its range of risk management products, although revenue from information management systems provider TIBCO was held back as it introduced a new product line to extend its activities beyond the trading floor.

Growth in recurring revenue from information products was broadly maintained and showed a 7 percent rise for the first nine months, while Instinet, the equities trading system, achieved a 46 percent rise in revenue during the period, which saw a number of record trading days.

Reuters said currency markets generally remained featureless, holding back foreign exchange dealing services, while media revenue was affected by the disposal of London Radio. Job said heavy investment in the company's product line required the streamlining of its organisation to achieve maximum market penetration in a cost-effective manner.

"We have begun that process with the recent announcements of changes to the management structure. The changes are intended to produce a more precise delineation of production and commercial functions in the company," he said.

Job said the company aimed to "integrate our architecture, simplify the production and administration of our products, and increase the competitive advantage that our large editorial organisation gives us in enabling us to produce and exploit broader and deeper global content.
"We expect to achieve a sharper focus on our media and other non-finance products and make use of our most promising new business opportunities rapidly," he added.
